clue.text: Complacent son, soft touch

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees
a mug is a gullible person, easy to exploit

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied boy who is easily taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone smugly pleased with themselves and untroubled by doubt.

clue.text: Covers one with peppery seeds

parts.note: caps are covers or lids
I is the Roman numeral for one
cum is Latin for with, as in 'bedroom-cum-study'

explanation.surface: Lids placed over something seasoned with spicy seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link here: it is the Latin CUM, used in English for 'combined with'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capsicum is the pepper plant, whose fruit holds hot, pungent seeds.

clue.text: Adjusted TV near bar

indicators.note: adjusting the letters of the words given sets them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tweaking the television set close to the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusted' rearranges the letters of TV NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or pub, a bar serving drinks.

clue.text: Mate in Italian city hugging daughter — Anna, perhaps

parts.note: a pal is a friend or mate

indicators.note: the words in and the Italian city wrap their arms around the daughter's letter

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A friend in an Italian city embracing a daughter named Anna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anna' reads as a woman's name in the scene; 'perhaps' flags her as just one example of the category, a name that runs the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Anna reads the same backwards as forwards, making it an example of a word symmetrical in spelling.

clue.text: Greek character hosting a dance

indicators.note: a host contains guests, so the Greek letter holds the other piece within it

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man throwing a party with dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person; it is the letter LAMBDA, which takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance popular around 1990.

clue.text: Acquire a knowledge of humorist and knight

parts.note: Edward Lear was the Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Getting to know a comic writer and a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to gain understanding of it through study or experience.

clue.text: Where lots go to join game

parts.note: lots are the items put up for sale at an auction
to bridge is to connect or link two things

explanation.surface: A place where many people head to take part in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' reads as 'many people' but means sale items.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is an older form of the card game, in which contracts were bid for.

clue.text: A role not being taken into account

parts.note: an actor's part is the role played

explanation.surface: An actor's role that gets ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'joking apart', the word means setting something aside, leaving it out of consideration.

clue.text: Article on pitch in Gibraltar

parts.note: the is the definite article
a ship that pitches rocks to and fro

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a playing field in Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field; it is the verb, to sway as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar is popularly nicknamed after its great limestone promontory.

clue.text: Groups of workers across English river

indicators.note: the gangs stretch across, spanning the other letter so it sits within them

parts.note: gangs are teams of labourers

explanation.surface: Work teams crossing an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred river of northern India.

clue.text: Form of verse member of the clergy abridged, then cut

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a cleric is a priest or minister
to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: A clergyman's poem is shortened and then trimmed further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' drops the last C of CLERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line biographical poem, invented by E. C. Bentley.

clue.text: Check popular page in part of paper

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the page letter is placed in the middle of the newspaper part

parts.note: a section is a part of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Checking a well-liked page within a newspaper supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspection is an examination or check of something.

clue.text: New spares sent round have to meet a required standard

indicators.note: the rearranged spares are sent round the other piece, enclosing it
new means renewed or made over, so the letters of spares are reorganised

parts.note: must means have to

explanation.surface: Replacement parts dispatched must be up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the letters into PASSER, and 'sent round' has that wrap the modal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is an idiom from military inspection: to be judged acceptable.

clue.text: Ruin atmosphere in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mood is the prevailing atmosphere or feeling

explanation.surface: A sense of ruin hanging over an army falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is destruction or a terrible fate, the same as ruin.

clue.text: Game chap who delivers, opening in second innings

parts.note: a postman delivers mail

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: in cricket, a batsman's innings is called a knock

explanation.surface: A cricketer who delivers the ball opening the batting in the second innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivers' and 'innings' suggest a bowler at cricket. 'opening in' takes the S of 'second'.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman's knock is a children's party game where a 'postman' delivers letters in exchange for kisses.

clue.text: Cover charge?

parts.note: a cover charge is a restaurant fee, but here cover means insurance and the charge is what is paid for it

explanation.surface: The extra fee a restaurant adds to the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance premium is the regular payment that buys protection under a policy.

clue.text: Left fabulous ship south of central island

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed below, so after

parts.note: key means of central importance
the Argo was the legendary ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: A legendary ship abandoned to the south of an island in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Key Largo is one of the Florida Keys, a chain of small islands.

clue.text: Appear in court before foremost of magistrates

indicators.note: before places the court ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat or court

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Turning up in court in front of the magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' here is a see, the seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give an impression or look a certain way.

clue.text: They may relieve tension in derby as row breaks out

indicators.note: something breaking out bursts apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Something calming at a local football match when a fight erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks out' rearranges DERBY AS ROW. A derby is a match between local rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Worry beads are a string of beads fingered to calm nerves and ease stress.

clue.text: Treacherous type in West stand

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A traitor hidden among the crowd in a western grandstand.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, deceitful person, named after the animal's sneaky reputation.

clue.text: The old man ringing about object of fear

indicators.note: the father's letters encircle the other piece like a ring

parts.note: the old man is slang for one's father, dad
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A father telephoning about something frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like telephoning but means encircling.
explanation.definitionFit: A dread can be a thing feared, a source of terror or apprehension.

clue.text: Female diarist shot, gets immediate attention

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman keeping a diary is shot and is treated at once.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the emergency treatment given straight away to an injured person.

clue.text: Accepted elderly must imbibe red, mostly

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: aged means old or elderly

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Old folk are expected to drink red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts RED to RE, which AGED drinks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed and accepted both mean consented to or approved.

clue.text: Artist capturing male bird that can't fly

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the other piece goes in

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A painter catching a bird that is grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American ratite, like a small ostrich.

clue.text: Private detective I use is rubbish!

parts.note: what I use belongs to me, so it is described as my own
a private eye is a private detective, so eye alone stands for one

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing the private investigator they hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private detective' suggests PRIVATE EYE; only EYE is wanted, with MY for what 'I use'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an old-fashioned way of saying 'nonsense!'.

clue.text: For example, leader of group, chief boffin

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the head is the chief

explanation.surface: A team leader who is also the top scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or brainy intellectual.
